obligations.note: is_allowed now allows any action string that starts with "report:" whenever the role holds the stripped name, so those pairs are not explicit grants and are outside the approved matrix. Default-deny no longer holds for that prefix, and the passing matrix test only covers the declared role-action list.

The auditor's grants are only view_account, view_audit, view_reports, and export_ledger, none of which are state-changing, and the prefix alias only repeats those grants. The exhaustive auditor control test passed on the head commit.

it_admin is granted manage_users, rotate_keys, purge_npi, and view_audit only, so approve_payment and release_payment stay denied even as report: aliases. The exhaustive segregation control test passed on the head commit.
Ticket CHG-24775 is approved by change manager Erik Brandt before review time and lists payments.access, the component of the only changed file, rbac.py.
Mara Costa, a payments change approver and not the author Sofia Santos, approved a code review of the head commit.
The change is a single commit, and both the code review and the security review name that commit, 82712f6d.

records/ci/run.json records a successful payments suite on the head commit, and the JUnit report shows 172 tests with no failures, errors, or skips, including the registered ACC-1, ACC-2, and SOD-1 control tests.
rbac.py is security-sensitive, and Kofi Mensah, a security reviewer who is not the author, approved a security review of the head commit.
The diff changes only apps/baseline-payments/payments/rbac.py, which is not a protected path, so a control-owner approval is not required.
The ticket type is standard and the change record is not an emergency, so a post-implementation review is not due.
The access-matrix deviation has no approved exception for ACC-1 or payments.access. The register entries are an expired session exception, a mortgage logging exception, and a withdrawn MFA exception.
The acceptance-ledger entries cover payments, audit, and routes code that this change does not modify, so that prior evidence has not lapsed.

summary: The change adds a report: prefix rewrite in payments is_allowed so a role is allowed any prefixed action whose stripped name is already granted. That is not an explicit matrix entry, it is not in the approved access policy, and it breaks default-deny for those names, so ACC-1 is violated. No valid exception covers that deviation. Ticket, independent code and security approvals, and a green suite on the head commit are in order, and the auditor and IT-admin restrictions still hold, but the access-matrix break blocks acceptance.
